0.long_answer: During embryologic development, the lateral plate mesoderm divides into two layers: the visceral (or splanchnic) layer and the parietal (or somatic) layer. The parietal layer, together with the overlying ectoderm, forms the lateral body wall. If the parietal layer does not develop properly, this can lead to a failure of the ventral body wall to fuse at the midline, thereby resulting in defects such as ectopia cordis, where the heart is abnormally positioned outside of the thoracic cavity.
0.short_answer: parietal layer of the lateral plate mesoderm
